decided.singular: Days 1, 121, 135, 174, 239, 296 and 365 each have a daily max far above their neighbours (85-117) while the daily mean stays modest. That points to short hourly bursts. 39-44, 65-71 and 78-84 are multi-day runs where the daily mean climbs to 40-65. 297-303 is an unusually low, flat run that starts right after the day-296 spike.
decided.highest: Q1 has all of the sustained high-mean runs (daily means of 40-65 in February and March), and no other quarter comes close.
decided.lowest: Q3 has the most days with means near 10-15 and only a few short bumps (225-227, 239, 252-253). Q4 and Q2 are close to it, so this is a narrow call.
decided.recurrence: In this per-day max and mean listing I could see no clear, consistent 5-10 day rhythm, and the episodic swings would hide one anyway.

answer.guess: Hourly particulate matter (PM10/PM2.5) concentration at an urban air-quality station. The spikes on New Year's Day and New Year's Eve fit fireworks, and the late-winter runs fit pollution episodes.
